title: Store refit programme: seven stores
bodyMd: A retail chain refitted seven of its stores last year. For each store the table gives the length of the refit, what the refit cost, and the average weekly footfall in the twelve weeks before the refit began and in the twelve weeks after it finished. The columns may be sorted in any order. Footfall figures are in thousands of visitors per week and refit costs are in thousands of euros.

data.caption: Seven refitted stores, with refit duration in weeks, refit cost in thousands of euros, and average weekly footfall in thousands before and after the refit.

accessibilityText: A sortable table of seven refitted stores with four measures each: refit duration in weeks, refit cost in thousands of euros, average weekly footfall before the refit in thousands, and average weekly footfall after the refit in thousands. Ashmere: 6 weeks, 420 thousand euros, 18.0 before, 22.5 after. Brantly: 9 weeks, 610 thousand euros, 24.0 before, 30.0 after. Cordell: 5 weeks, 380 thousand euros, 15.0 before, 17.7 after. Dunwold: 7 weeks, 455 thousand euros, 12.5 before, 15.5 after. Esgrove: 11 weeks, 740 thousand euros, 31.0 before, 34.1 after. Fanshaw: 4 weeks, 295 thousand euros, 9.0 before, 11.7 after. Garrick: 8 weeks, 490 thousand euros, 20.0 before, 24.0 after.

provenance.notes: Original table. Store names and every figure were invented for this bank. The before and after footfall pairs were chosen so that each store's percentage change is an exact value (25, 25, 18, 24, 10, 30 and 20 percent respectively), with Garrick sitting exactly on a 20 percent threshold so that a strict-inequality question has one defensible answer.
